overview.headline: Simplified aircraft motion with balanced and unbalanced forces

keyPoints.point: Simplified motion looks at one force and one direction at a time while other forces are balanced.
keyPoints.quote: some of the four forces acting on the aircraft are balanced by other forces

keyPoints.point: Constant speed level flight happens when weight is balanced by lift and drag is balanced by thrust.
keyPoints.quote: the weight would be balanced by the lift and the drag would be balanced by the thrust.

keyPoints.point: Newton’s second law lets you compute aircraft acceleration from the net force.
keyPoints.quote: We can compute the acceleration which the aircraft will experience from Newton’s second law of motion:

keyPoints.point: Net force is the difference between opposing forces like lift minus weight or thrust minus drag.
keyPoints.quote: The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.

keyTerms.gloss: downward force that is balanced by lift during level flight
keyTerms.quote: In an ideal situation, an airplane could sustain a constant speed and level flight in which the weight would be balanced by the lift
